channel.title: Wire — Ruby
channel.description: Ruby from thirty sources, one digest a day.

item.title: Neat Annotations: Elegant Hand-Drawn Annotations with CSS
item.description: Arrows and handwritten labels for your website. Pure CSS, no JavaScript. (2 sources: frontendfocus, rubyweekly)

item.title: May's RubyGems spam flood
item.description: GemStuffer abuses RubyGems as an exfiltration channel, packaging scraped UK council portal data into junk gems published from new accounts. (1 source: rubyweekly)

item.title: new and emerging HTML features worth knowing about
item.description: You've got your permissions elements, custom element registries, a potential future for HTML includes, HTML-in-Canvas, and a bunch more. (2 sources: javascriptweekly, rubyweekly)

item.title: OpenAI agents carried out an undisclosed attack on RubyGems
item.description: On May 11th, 2026, hundreds of malicious packages were uploaded to RubyGems by AI agents performing web-lookup tasks with significant overlap with the German Wiki Incident. (3 sources: hackernews, lobsters, rubyweekly)

item.title: Homebrew 7.0.0
item.description: Today, I’m proud to announce Homebrew 7.0.0. The most significant changes since 6.0.0 are faster installations and upgrades, stronger sandboxing, a native macOS app, built-in vulnerability checks and an advisory database, the end of macOS… (2 sources: lobsters, rubyweekly)

item.title: Ruby Central finds no evidence
item.description: Following reporting by The Wall Street Journal and the publication of research by Nightingale Collective, we want to clarify what we know about the spam-publishing campaign on rubygems.org in May 2... (1 source: rubyweekly)

item.title: disclosed the caching bug
item.description: A CDN caching bug on RubyGems.org could hand one account’s API key to another person for up to an hour. (1 source: rubyweekly)

item.title: digs into the code from May that targeted it
item.description: We discovered and reported a RubyGems vulnerability in July. Researchers now believe OpenAI agents had attempted to exploit it nearly two months earlier. (1 source: rubyweekly)

item.title: Upgrading Rails Is Dead Simple Now. So Why Are You Behind?
item.description: Get your Rails application current without taking your team off the roadmap. Senior-reviewed upgrades and security fixes, starting at $1,950/mo. (1 source: rubyweekly)
